title: Laying on of hands
hookLine: believers pray with a hand on the shoulder of the one prayed for

lines: A HOUSE ON THE STREET CALLED STRAIGHT.
THE MAN WHO CAME TO ARREST.
cards: In Damascus, a disciple named Ananias hears the Lord tell him to go to a house on the street called Straight and ask for a man named Saul. Ananias knows that name.
Saul has come to Damascus with authority to arrest people like him, and Ananias says so: he's heard how much evil this man has done. The answer comes back: go.
So he walks into the house where Saul sits blind, puts his hands on him, and says, "Brother Saul." Then something like scales falls from Saul's eyes, and he can see.

teach.b: Through the New Testament, hands carry prayer. When parents bring children to Jesus, Mark says, "he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them." Hands that bless.
When the church in Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul out, "when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away."
On Malta, when the father of Publius lay sick of a fever, Acts says Paul "entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him." Hands on the sick.
James, too, tells the sick to call the elders of the church to pray over them. Pentecostal and charismatic Christians keep this close.
When someone asks for prayer, others gather round, and a hand goes on a shoulder or a back while they pray, for healing, for strength, for the Holy Spirit.

Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican and other churches keep the gesture in their rites, and ordain their ministers with the laying on of hands. In these passages, the hands come with words: a blessing, a prayer, a name.
The prayer is to God; the hand says something to the person. Someone is with you, close enough to touch. Now go back to Ananias.
The hands on Saul belonged to a man with every reason to be afraid of him. Before Saul could see anything, he felt those hands, and heard himself called brother.
It closes the distance between people before it asks God for anything.

how: In Pentecostal and charismatic churches, people who ask for prayer are often surrounded by others who pray with a hand on their shoulder; Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican and other churches ordain ministers with the laying on of hands.

games.q: what does “laying on of hands” mean?
o: a blessing given only to children at baptism
a healing touch that works even without any prayer
praying with a hand resting on the person prayed for

games.q: hands and prayer — tap the pairs.
p: took the children in his arms and blessed them
fasted, prayed, laid hands, sent them
Paul prayed, laid hands on a sick man

s: laying on of hands is found only in Pentecostal churches
it runs through Mark and Acts, and churches ordain with it too.
Ananias laid his hands on Saul
"Brother Saul." and Saul could see again.
in today's passages, the hands work without prayer
in Mark and Acts, the hands come with blessing, prayer or a spoken word.

games.q: you're Ananias. the Lord tells you to go to Saul, the man who came to Damascus to arrest believers like you. what do you do?
o: go, put your hands on him, and call him brother.
send someone else in your place.
games.why: Ananias objects first, then goes. he lays his hands on Saul and says, "Brother Saul." something like scales falls from Saul's eyes.

practice: If someone you're close to is nearby, ask first whether you may pray for them or hold them in mind, and with a yes, rest a hand lightly on their shoulder; if you're alone, bring someone to mind and rest your own hand over your heart.
If you pray, pray for them in your own words, or simply say their name before God. If you don't, hold them with care, gently and briefly.

wordCard.voice: Laying on of hands. Praying with a hand resting on the person prayed for: to bless, to heal, to send, and to say someone is with you.

orig.note: Greek: the laying on of hands, the phrase in 1 Timothy 4:14.

carryVoice: Your line: a hand and a prayer. Ananias called him brother first. See you tomorrow.
